newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Jan retail sales rise 1.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Canada Jan retail sales rise 1.4 pct.

text.p: Canadian retail sales rose 1.4 percent in January to a seasonally adjusted C$18.79 billion from a revised C$18.54 billion (C$18.45 billion) in December, Statistics Canada said on Thursday.
Sales, ex vehicles, s/a +2.2 +4.6 C$14.21 bln
Statistics Canada said early indications for February sales were for a rise in the number of new motor vehicles sold.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast a 0.4 percent rise in retail sales in January after December's 0.3 percent fall.

Statistics Canada said the large increase in sales was spurred by consumers in British Columbia, who returned to the stores in January after harsh weather in December. Excluding British Columbia, total retail sales rose by only 0.1 percent in January, Statscan said.
The January increases were broad-based, with sales rising in six out of seven retail sectors, the agency said. Only general merchandise stories saw a decline in sales, with a fall of 0.5 percent.

In the automotive sector, increasing sales in automotive parts, accessories and services as well as gasoline service stations were able to offset the falling sales of recreational and motor vehicle dealers, said Statscan.

Sales in the food sector rose 2.0 percent, the second rise in two months. But general merchandise sales declined for the second straight month, despite a 1.4 percent increase in deparment store sales, the agency said.
